prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To generate an actual dollar estimate I would need: (1) the appraised value (or competing appraisals) of the strip of land UDOT actually took, including its square footage/acreage; (2) Boggess's own expert's stated dollar figure for claimed severance damages (the diminished-access/increased-traffic impairment), not just the theory; (3) the total square footage of the remainder parcel, so the $8.75-to-$12.50 per-square-foot before/after swing UDOT's expert relies on can actually be converted into a total dollar figure comparable to Boggess's claim; and (4) the amount (if disclosed anywhere) of the first jury's vacated verdict, which would at least provide a benchmark for how a jury has previously valued these same components before the evidentiary rules changed.
prediction.likelyOutcome: Boggess will recover just compensation for the land physically taken (essentially uncontested as to entitlement) and will likely obtain some award for severance damages given its theory survived to a first verdict, but the retrial evidentiary landscape -- admission of the 2016 sale/development and the pretrial ruling that UDOT's claimed benefits are 'special' rather than 'general' -- meaningfully favors UDOT relative to the first trial and creates real risk that the jury substantially discounts or offsets the severance component against UDOT's $2.2 million special-benefits theory. Without the underlying appraisal figures or Boggess's own damages claim in the record, I cannot respons­ibly quantify a net number, but directionally this reads as a case where Boggess still wins something meaningful on the land-value component while facing a live, material battle over how much (if any) severance damages survive the special-benefits offset.

issues.label: Entitlement to Just Compensation for Land Taken
Severance Damages Claim (Diminished Access / Increased Traffic)
Admissibility of Post-Valuation Sale and Development Evidence
Exclusion of the 2016 Sale Price (Rule 403 Partial Win)
Retrial Risk From the First Verdict's Reversal

outcome.description: On retrial the jury awarded Boggess approximately $330,000 (the opinion gives only this rounded figure) for the value of the condemned property and found no severance damages, after UDOT's expert was allowed to testify to a $2.2 million project-benefit offset. The Court of Appeals held that interstate access and added travel lanes are general benefits that cannot offset severance damages, found the error harmful, reversed the verdict and remanded for a new trial; no fees are discussed.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed for a new trial; no final figure yet.
